nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong sun powers algae on the open mud and in the shallow water, though summer heat and drying also stress life on the flats.

nodes.name: Tidal flooding
nodes.desc: Seawater floods and drains the low mudflats and salt marshes, bringing food in and exposing invertebrates to wading birds at low tide.

nodes.name: Delta silt and nutrients
nodes.desc: Sediment from the Tigris-Euphrates river system built the muddy delta coast of the northern Gulf, and river water carries nutrients to the bays.

nodes.name: Bacteria and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead algae, plants and animals in the mud and return nutrients to the water and sediment.

nodes.name: Phytoplankton
nodes.desc: Drifting microscopic algae that feed on nutrient-rich water and form the base of the open-water food chain.

nodes.name: Benthic diatoms
nodes.desc: Microscopic algae that coat the surface of the mud; this film is grazed by mudskippers and other mudflat animals.

nodes.name: Saltmarsh glasswort
nodes.desc: A salt-tolerant shrub of saline coastal marshes around the Persian Gulf, which binds salty ground at the edge of the tidal flats.

nodes.name: Copepods
nodes.desc: Tiny crustaceans that graze phytoplankton in the water and are food for small fish.

nodes.name: Marine worms
nodes.desc: Bristle worms living in the mud, a major prey of shorebirds that probe the flats.

nodes.name: Green tiger prawn
nodes.desc: A prawn of sandy and muddy coastal waters whose juveniles favour estuaries; a commercially important species in the region.

nodes.name: Sentinel crabs
nodes.desc: A genus of soft-bottom crabs living on tidal flats of the Indo-Pacific, hunted by shorebirds that specialise on crabs.

nodes.name: Mudskipper
nodes.desc: Fish that crawls over mudflats at low tide scraping green algae, and is also found in Kuwait Sulaibikhat Bay.

nodes.name: Flathead grey mullet
nodes.desc: A widespread coastal fish that feeds on algae, detritus and tiny animals from bottom mud.

nodes.name: Western reef heron
nodes.desc: Wades in shallows for fish, crustaceans and molluscs; on coasts mudskippers are a regular part of its diet.

nodes.name: Grey heron
nodes.desc: Large wading bird that stalks fish in shallow water and is a common winter visitor on Gulf coasts.

nodes.name: Dunlin
nodes.desc: Small wintering shorebird that probes mudflats in flocks for molluscs, worms and crustaceans.

nodes.name: Eurasian curlew
nodes.desc: Large wader whose long curved bill reaches worms and crabs buried in soft mud.

nodes.name: Crab-plover
nodes.desc: A crab specialist that nests in burrows in sandy banks; Bubiyan reportedly hosts the largest breeding colony in the world.

nodes.name: Caspian tern
nodes.desc: Large tern that plunges for fish, hunting over bays and sometimes travelling far from its colony to feed.

nodes.name: Indian Ocean humpback dolphin
nodes.desc: A shallow coastal dolphin that mostly eats sciaenid fish, cephalopods and crustaceans.

nodes.name: Osprey
nodes.desc: A fish-eating raptor that dives for fish in shallow coastal water.
